Her family said the cause of death was rhabdomyolysis, a rare side effect of hard exercise. Rhabdo can afflict even experienced athletes and cause life-threatening symptoms if left untreated. A 24-year-old woman who died after the New York City Marathon on Sunday was suffering from a rare side effect of exercise called rhabdomyolysis, her family said. Rachel Apa, an experienced D1 field hockey athlete who spent months training for the race, collapsed near mile 24 in Central Park and was taken by ambulance to the hospital, her father told The New York Times . Apa was a product manager for an electronic manufacturing company. Earlier this year, she posted on LinkedIn that she was running the marathon to raise money for the Parkinson's Foundation, in honor of her grandfather.
